raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

With `--tool-call-parser kimi_k3`, a streaming chat completion emits **no chunks while the model is generating a tool call**. The whole call (name + all arguments) is delivered as one `tool_calls` delta after `<|close|>call<|sep|>`. For agentic workloads where a call carries a whole file (`write_file` with thousands of tokens of `content`), the stream is silent for minutes; proxies with a per-chunk idle timeout (300 s in our deployment) kill the request and the generation is wasted. Details and a client-side timeline are in #45697.

Root cause: `KimiK3Detector.parse_streaming_increment` re-runs `_CALL_RE` over the whole buffer on every chunk, and that regex only matches a complete call. Most other detectors (`kimi_k2`, `qwen25`, `deepseekv31`, `glm47`) emit the name early and then stream `arguments` fragments.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/function_call/kimik3_detector.py`, streaming path only:

- Replace the whole-call regex with a state machine over the XTML nesting (tools channel > call > argument value). Each state consumes one marker or a run of text at a time; the buffer is trimmed after every increment, so scanning is incremental.
- Emit a `ToolCallItem` with the name and empty parameters as soon as `<|open|>call tool="x" ...<|sep|>` is complete.
- `type="string"` arguments stream as they arrive: `{"key": "` / `, "key": "` on the open tag, `json.dumps(fragment)[1:-1]` for each text fragment (per-character escaping, so fragments concatenate to the escaped whole), `"` on the close tag. A suffix that could start a close marker is held back via the existing `partial_suffix_len`.
- Non-string arguments are emitted when they close (they need `json.loads`/`json.dumps` normalisation, and are short).
- `}` on `<|close|>call<|sep|>`. The concatenation of all fragments is byte-identical to `detect_and_parse`'s `parameters`, so `prev_tool_call_arr` / `streamed_args_for_tool` keep their contract with `serving_chat._check_for_unstreamed_tool_args` (it finds nothing left to send).
- A call cut off by end of stream or by `<|close|>tools<|sep|>` has its JSON closed (`"` and `}`) instead of being left as a dangling prefix; `detect_and_parse` drops such a call, but streaming has already sent its name. Logged at WARNING.
- Nameless calls are skipped without consuming a tool index, matching `detect_and_parse`.

`detect_and_parse` (non-streaming) is unchanged.

`test/registered/function_call/test_kimik3_detector.py`:

- Existing streaming tests now fold fragments per tool index before asserting.
- New: 300 seeded random-chunking cases asserting streamed output == `detect_and_parse` and the bookkeeping arrays; name + argument fragments arrive before the call closes; partial close marker held back; nameless call skipped; truncated call closed.

## Accuracy Tests

No model forward changes. Parser equivalence, checked offline:

- **Differential fuzz against the model's own renderer** (`encoding_k3.py` from the Kimi-K3 repo renders random OpenAI-style tool calls to XTML; the real K3 tokenizer splits it; chunks of 1 token, whole text, random 1–6 token groups, and single characters are fed through `ReasoningParser("kimi_k3")` → `FunctionCallParser` → the serving layer's completion check; 30 % of cases are truncated inside the tools channel). 4 seeds × 3000 messages = 144,000 streaming replays, 0 failures. Argument values deliberately include quotes, backslashes, control characters, CJK, emoji, `&`/`"`, and partial and complete `<|open|>`/`<|close|>`/`<|sep|>` markers. Per step it also asserts the name is sent once, fragments belong to the current tool, and the streamed prefix is always a JSON prefix.
- 1500 marker-free realistic calls (code in `content`): streamed arguments byte-identical to the renderer input in all 18,000 replays.
- Unit suites touching the parser chain (`test_serving_chat`, `test_serving_responses`, `test_kimik3_reasoning_parser`, `test_kimik3_structural_tag`, `test_kimik2_detector`, `test_function_call_parser`, `test_kimik3_detector`): 959 passed.

Known, intended differences from `detect_and_parse`: a call truncated mid-argument is kept and closed (non-streaming drops it); duplicate keys are all streamed (a JSON decoder keeps the last, as the non-streaming dict does).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Parser-only, replaying a single `write_file` call in 4-char chunks:

| `content` length | old (µs/chunk) | new (µs/chunk) |
|---|---|---|
| 10k chars | 30 | 2.7 |
| 100k chars | 212 | 8.3 |
| 400k chars | 887 | 14 |

Simulated client timeline for the #45697 repro shape (≈4k tokens at 11 ms/token): first tool-call byte 45.0 s → 0.2 s after the call starts; longest silence 45.0 s → 0.25 s. Not yet verified end-to-end on a GPU server; I will add that before taking this out of draft.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

     return {m["k"]: _unescape_attr(m["v"]) for m in _ATTR_RE.finditer(attrs)}
 
 
+_SEP = "<|sep|>"
+_ARGUMENT_OPEN = "<|open|>argument"
+
+# Streaming states, mirroring the nesting _CALL_RE / _ARG_RE match.
+_NORMAL = "normal"  # before the tools channel
+_TOOLS = "tools"  # inside the tools channel, between calls
+_CALL = "call"  # inside a call, between arguments
+_VALUE = "value"  # inside an argument value
+_SKIP_CALL = "skip_call"  # inside a call with no tool name
+_DONE = "done"  # tools channel closed; the rest is ignored
+
+_NO_MATCH = object()
+
+
+def _json_str_body(text: str) -> str:
+    # json.dumps escapes per character, so escaped fragments concatenate to the
+    # escaped whole.
+    return json.dumps(text, ensure_ascii=False)[1:-1]
+
+
+def _first_marker(text: str, pos: int, markers: List[str]) -> tuple[int, str | None]:
+    best_idx, best_marker = -1, None
+    for marker in markers:
+        idx = text.find(marker, pos)
+        if idx != -1 and (best_idx == -1 or idx < best_idx):
+            best_idx, best_marker = idx, marker
+    return best_idx, best_marker
+
+
+def _hold(buf: str, pos: int, markers: List[str]) -> int:
+    """End of the text that cannot be the start of one of ``markers``."""
+    return max(pos, len(buf) - partial_suffix_len(buf, markers))
+
+
+def _read_open_tag(buf: str, idx: int, prefix: str, fences: List[str]):
+    """Parse ``prefix\\s+attrs<|sep|>`` at ``idx`` like _CALL_RE / _ARG_RE do.
+
+    Returns (attrs, end) on a match, None if more text is needed, or _NO_MATCH
+    if the regex would not match here (no whitespace, or a fence comes first).
+    """
+    start = idx + len(prefix)
+    if start >= len(buf):
+        return None
+    if not buf[start].isspace():
+        return _NO_MATCH
+    sep = buf.find(_SEP, start)
+    if sep == -1:
+        return None
+    for fence in fences:
+        fence_idx = buf.find(fence, start)
+        if fence_idx != -1 and fence_idx < sep:
+            return _NO_MATCH
+    return buf[start:sep], sep + len(_SEP)
+

+            pending = self._emit_normal_text(limit=len(self._buffer))

+                normal_text=strip_partial_marker_suffix(pending)
+            )
+        calls: List[ToolCallItem] = []
+        if self._state in (_CALL, _VALUE):
+            logger.warning(
+                "Kimi K3 stream ended inside tool call %d; closing its arguments",
+                self.current_tool_id,
+            )

+        elif self.current_tool_id == -1:

+                "Kimi K3 tools section ended with no complete tool call; "
+                "dropping %d buffered chars",
+                len(self._buffer),

+
+    # ===== Streaming state machine (tools channel) =====
+
+    def _advance(self) -> List[ToolCallItem]:
+        out: List[ToolCallItem] = []
+        buf, pos, progressed = self._buffer, 0, True
+        while progressed and self._state != _DONE:
+            pos, progressed = self._step(buf=buf, pos=pos, out=out)
+        self._buffer = "" if self._state == _DONE else buf[pos:]
+        return out
+
+    def _step(self, buf: str, pos: int, out: List[ToolCallItem]) -> tuple[int, bool]:
+        """Consume one marker or a run of text; return (new_pos, progressed)."""
+        if self._state == _TOOLS:
+            return self._step_tools(buf=buf, pos=pos, out=out)
+        if self._state == _CALL:
+            return self._step_call(buf=buf, pos=pos, out=out)
+        if self._state == _VALUE:
+            return self._step_value(buf=buf, pos=pos, out=out)
+        return self._step_skip_call(buf=buf, pos=pos)
+
+    def _step_tools(
+        self, buf: str, pos: int, out: List[ToolCallItem]
+    ) -> tuple[int, bool]:
+        markers = [CALL_OPEN, TOOLS_CLOSE]
+        idx, marker = _first_marker(buf, pos, markers)
+        if marker is None:
+            return _hold(buf=buf, pos=pos, markers=markers), False
+        if marker == TOOLS_CLOSE:
+            self._state = _DONE
+            return len(buf), False
+        tag = _read_open_tag(buf=buf, idx=idx, prefix=CALL_OPEN, fences=[TOOLS_CLOSE])
+        if tag is None:
+            return idx, False
+        if tag is _NO_MATCH:
+            return idx + 1, True
+        attrs, end = tag
+        name = _parse_attrs(attrs).get("tool", "")
+        if name:
+            self._start_call(name=name, out=out)
+            self._state = _CALL
+        else:
+            # detect_and_parse drops nameless calls without consuming an index.
+            self._state = _SKIP_CALL
+        return end, True
+
+    def _step_call(
+        self, buf: str, pos: int, out: List[ToolCallItem]
+    ) -> tuple[int, bool]:
+        markers = [_ARGUMENT_OPEN, CALL_CLOSE, TOOLS_CLOSE]
+        idx, marker = _first_marker(buf, pos, markers)
+        if marker is None:
+            return _hold(buf=buf, pos=pos, markers=markers), False
+        if marker == TOOLS_CLOSE:
+            logger.warning(
+                "Kimi K3 tools channel closed inside tool call %d; "
+                "closing its arguments",
+                self.current_tool_id,
+            )
+            self._abort_call(out=out)
+            self._state = _DONE
+            return len(buf), False
+        if marker == CALL_CLOSE:
+            self._finish_call(out=out)
+            self._state = _TOOLS
+            return idx + len(CALL_CLOSE), True
+        tag = _read_open_tag(
+            buf=buf, idx=idx, prefix=_ARGUMENT_OPEN, fences=[CALL_CLOSE, TOOLS_CLOSE]
+        )
+        if tag is None:
+            return idx, False
+        if tag is _NO_MATCH:
+            return idx + 1, True
+        attrs, end = tag
+        self._start_argument(attrs=attrs, out=out)
+        self._state = _VALUE
+        return end, True
+
+    def _step_value(
+        self, buf: str, pos: int, out: List[ToolCallItem]
+    ) -> tuple[int, bool]:
+        markers = [ARGUMENT_CLOSE, CALL_CLOSE, TOOLS_CLOSE]
+        idx, marker = _first_marker(buf, pos, markers)
+        if marker is None:
+            safe = _hold(buf=buf, pos=pos, markers=markers)
+            self._append_value(text=buf[pos:safe], out=out)
+            return safe, False
+        self._append_value(text=buf[pos:idx], out=out)
+        self._state = _CALL
+        if marker == ARGUMENT_CLOSE:
+            self._end_argument(out=out)
+            return idx + len(ARGUMENT_CLOSE), True
+        self._drop_argument(out=out)
+        return idx, True
+
+    def _step_skip_call(self, buf: str, pos: int) -> tuple[int, bool]:
+        markers = [CALL_CLOSE, TOOLS_CLOSE]
+        idx, marker = _first_marker(buf, pos, markers)
+        if marker is None:
+            return _hold(buf=buf, pos=pos, markers=markers), False
+        if marker == TOOLS_CLOSE:
+            self._state = _DONE
+            return len(buf), False
+        self._state = _TOOLS
+        return idx + len(CALL_CLOSE), True
+
+    def _start_call(self, name: str, out: List[ToolCallItem]) -> None:
+        self.current_tool_id += 1
+        while len(self.prev_tool_call_arr) <= self.current_tool_id:
+            self.prev_tool_call_arr.append({})
+        while len(self.streamed_args_for_tool) <= self.current_tool_id:
+            self.streamed_args_for_tool.append("")
+        self._call_name = name
+        self._call_args = {}
+        self._call_arg_count = 0
+        out.append(
+            ToolCallItem(tool_index=self.current_tool_id, name=name, parameters="")
